title: Row-level policy 9-matrix integration test
description: Proves that pkg/security.Engine compiled into Bleve queries filters rows correctly through the real oss.ServiceImpl Load path by exercising a 3-user × 3-policy × 5-object matrix end-to-end. Each cell issues ListObjects as a different user with a different active policy (eq / in / markingSubset), and asserts the exact primary key set returned by Bleve. The same 5-object fixture is reused across all three policy regimes — SetPolicies swaps the rule list in place and bumps the per-ObjectType version counter, invalidating any cached compilation from the prior cell so a stale cache cannot leak rows between regimes.

sequence: For each policyId in [eq, in, markingSubset]: engine.SetPolicies(employee.RID, rules[policyId])
For each userId in [alice, bob, carol]: svc.ListObjects(ctx{user=userId}, {ontology, objectType=employee, pageSize=50})
Collect returned WireObject.PrimaryKey values and assert the exact set matches the matrix expectation

expected.cacheInvariant: engine.SetPolicies bumps the per-ObjectType version counter and drops cached compilation entries, so swapping policyId between matrix cells never leaks a stale Bleve query from the prior regime into the next assertion
expected.failClosed: A user missing the referenced userAttr (e.g. no markings / no regions / no deptId) would compile to MatchNone — the nine-matrix does not exercise this branch because every user has every attribute; pkg/oss/policy_engine_integration_test.go::TestPolicyAppliedToLoadSearch_FailClosed covers the fallback

ListObjects.data: []WireObject — each row exposes $primaryKey / $apiName / $rid plus the selected properties
ListObjects.totalCount: string — reflects Bleve result.Total AFTER policy filtering (policy is AND-merged into the base query, so denied rows never count)

notes: Run with `go test -tags integration ./test/integration/... -run PolicyMatrix`. Requires Docker for testcontainers.

The `in` rule compiles to a BooleanQuery whose Should clauses are TermQuery(value, field=objectProperty) one per user value, MinShould=1 — for a multi-valued object field Bleve indexes each element as an independent term, so the Should matches any overlap.

The `markingSubset` rule currently reuses the same Should-terms shape with MinShould=1. For a single-valued object classification field this is exact subset semantics. Multi-valued object marking fields need the markings_sig index from US-058 to enforce true ⊆; that path is explicitly out of scope for this matrix.

All fields must be indexed as `analyzer: not_analyzed` so compileRule's TermQuery payloads match verbatim. Default English snowball analyzers silently break TermQuery-based policy clauses — Phase 6 learnings cover the same landmine.

The matrix exercises the ServiceImpl.ListObjects path. The ObjectSet executor's separate policy_provider hook (cmd/server/policy_provider.go + objectset.Executor.SetPolicyProvider) is covered independently by pkg/oss/objectset policy tests and does not need a duplicate matrix here.
